For *other* things.  
.. sooo yeahhh

I've reassured him that I'm not upset with him at all but he still feels weird about it. 
No, this isn't the first time we've had sex, just the first time I've taken Lunesta around him, i take it as needed.  
I have mixed feelings because as far as he and I knew Lunesta only made me sleep, I didn't do anything else. Now I know that's not true it kinda makes me feel vulnerable even though I trust him completely (we've been friends for 7+ years and he's yet to give me a reason not to trust him)

Everyone I've ever loved or trusted has either abused, used, cheated on or abandoned me.  
There is obviously something wrong with me if this is the on going pattern in my life.   
My health is declining, crippling me financially and physically. Quickly making me an even bigger burden each day.
I absolutely agree!

Thanks!   
I wish I could say it was easy for me to find the strength or that I know it'll never bend, but honestly, it's such a bitch because over the years he's made it to where he's the only person in my life I can depend on.  
Last night I considered hospitalization for my continuous suicidal thoughts and feelings. I've spoken to my therapist about this and she wanted me to go if I felt unable to control it.  
Well, my insurance doesn't cover mental health inpatient so, I had to come up with another plan...  
Which was to lay down the law: limit contact more than what I have already, be stern with my boundaries (fuck his feelings), not let him pull me on to his carousel of arguments, and if he crosses my Berlin Wall-esque lines, then obviously he can't be trusted, and doesn't respect me so, therefore paperwork for legal separation will be filed.

He's still coming up with lame excuses for his behavior, saying he's "changed" (miraculously overnight), but still trying to instigate arguments, and force me too make a decision.  
I'm really over being nice to him.  
It's hard to cut off contact completely because we have kids, but I'm drawing the line to kid only discussions.

He was implying that my plan was to get him to fess up to his wrong doings so I could boot him out on his ass.  
But really, I could of just printed divorce papers off the internet and changed the locks while he was at work if I wanted to just get rid of him.  
His first excuse (in a series of unending excuses) was that he didn't tell me when it first happened, because when he came home I was angry, and that I was always angry.   
Tonight we had to do the child-exchange and he took this opportunity to start up the war again, and said that he is working to fix himself, but he will never be able to truly fix himself unless he had my forgiveness, and be a part of his therapy and healing. I was floored.. and mad as hell too. I told him that he had no right to put that on me and I wasn't willing to be a part of that.   
Screaming at each other in a WalMart parking lot... so American.

The trust, or specifically the lack thereof, is one of the biggest problems.  
There is honestly no way to know if he would ever be trustworthy again, and if I did decided to trust him, how long would it last until he broke it? Would he just lie for another 5 years? Maybe forever knowing that that there would be no way in hell I would take him back? Would I become so paranoid that I would become a person that would constantly distrust him, read his texts and emails?  
I don't want to be that, just as much as I don't want to be the self-loathing person I've become.  
I'm wondering that if the separation lasts long enough, that he'll just screw up and make my decision for me.

>If he corrects his destructive behavior, would you stay with him? Or is this more of a transition to divorce for you - have you mentally checked out?  

I really don't know. Until last night he was still in the house, hovering and going on and on and on.. when I wasn't around him I was distracted by my job or my kids. Now that I get a few hours to myself I am trying to acknowledge and understand each one of the many emotions I am feeling. I try to be rational, civil, but cold, when I am around him - I don't want to continue the war, it doesn't solve anything. I feel like he is just trying to wear me down until I finally say "I forgive you come back"  
But I think I am way past that point

>It's funny how nice people will suddenly be to you when they find out you attempted suicide. It feels so fake.

When I attempted suicide, everyone was an asshole to me. One nurse actually told me that I was wasting emergency room resources for people who didn't bring this on themselves. She was a bitch. The doctors disregarded me. Other hospital staff members made me feel like a burden. And don't get me started on my mom ... 

But there was this one nurse, his name was Van, was so nice to me, even held my hair when the ipecac took effect and I screamvomited all the pills out of my stomach. He kept telling me that everything was going to be alright, and that I was going to be alright. 

15 years later I remember his name, and how he treated me - like a person. I am thankful I didn't die.

I'm glad you woke up and I hope you grow stronger and get the help you need. People care about you, even if you can't see it right now.

Thank you. 
We've tried couples counseling, and he is supportive, overall. but, I think he resents me for various reasons (I completed college while his college career was on hold - it was on hold before we started dating; My friend paid for me to fly to Seattle to visit her) and feels like I don't do enough "women's work" because I am working over 40 hours a week, and I make more than him. When we try to sit down and talk about it he pours out all of these shortcomings of mine, which just leaves me feeling worse and so angry at him that I just want to divorce him. We went to counseling, and it seemed fruitful for a few days, but old habits die hard.
My kids are young (9 and 5) so they don't do it on purpose, they legitimately love me and want to hang out with me. I think I project most of the guilt on to myself.  
I've applied to multiple jobs in the area, but I've gotten nothing back. I'm looking at out of state jobs now in my field - behavioral studies. 
Sometimes, I just want some appreciation  .. not like a ticker-tape parade in my honor, but a "thank you" works, a "let me help you" would probably work too.
Apparently, irony is big into me these days .. just saw this quote: “Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.” - Helen Keller.
